assessment_kind: Fresh targeted assessment; no earlier G02 output recovered
provenance: Assessor also implemented preceding G01 source changes; no independent acceptance asserted. Assessment documents published on docs/g02-authorization-audit-20261111 through a draft documentation PR; no application fixes, separate tracking issue or coordination policy created.

findings.requirement: Reconcile runtime policy and enforce reviewer project/resource scope
findings.acceptance: Unassigned reviewer list/detail/package metadata and artifact routes deny without existence disclosure; assigned, applicable reviewer access succeeds; other tenants remain inaccessible. Cover all org/project role combinations and capability-presence disagreements, including document.reuse and submission.recipients_manage. Resolve documented policy ambiguity through accountable review. The demonstrated exposure is package metadata; no signed download or ready artifact was tested.
findings.evidence_level: TARGETED_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION; see report for HTTP versus guard/service limits; not independent acceptance

findings.acceptance: Allowed asset/requirement succeeds; another asset/requirement, mixed bulk request and indirect document links deny atomically. Exercise read-only/date/type/category scopes and update/removal races. This probe used real guards/services and PostgreSQL, not an HTTP PATCH.
findings.evidence_level: TARGETED_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION; see report for HTTP versus guard/service limits; not independent acceptance

findings.requirement: Filter guest requirement rows before serialization
findings.acceptance: A-only supplier sees only A, including totals, pagination, filters and search; B, other suppliers and another tenant never appear. Empty scope and revoked/expired grants deny. Include upload-only and contributor profiles without making them project browsers.

findings.acceptance: Allowed linkage succeeds; unassigned, non-owned, cross-project and cross-tenant inputs deny without partial writes. findings.requirement: Separate grant issuance from supplier upload
findings.acceptance: Authorized contractor issuance works. Suppliers cannot mint scope B, choose another party, prolong authority or reassign obligations. Denied issuance writes no grant/assignment/outbox event. Include revocation and closed-project races. No external invitation was sent in this audit.

findings.requirement: Protect contractor intake and evidence eligibility
findings.acceptance: Supplier self-intake, unassigned/mismatched versions, null evidence, PROCESSING/quarantined/deleted versions and stale state deny. A properly authorized contractor accepts a legitimately submitted eligible version. Rejection, retries, concurrency and invalidation preserve correct status and history. Coordinate evidence semantics with the relevant document/procurement group; do not silently declare acceptance from this fixture.

Cover aliases, nested objects, unknown payloads, counts and projection context. Do not infer that every commercial-field projection has failed; the demonstrated leak is the member roster.

findings.requirement: Bind nested upload completion to the actual resource project
findings.acceptance: Authorized A/A completion succeeds; A/B and foreign-tenant tuples deny identically on all aliases. Exercise PENDING completion with actual isolated object fixtures, as well as PROCESSING/replay paths. This finding reproduced metadata exposure through the PROCESSING idempotent path; pending-upload storage mutation was not tested.

findings.requirement: Recheck current project authority under the mutation lock
findings.acceptance: A removal or demotion committed before the authoritative transaction check prevents the write. A write already inside the documented protected boundary either serializes before removal or fails consistently. Test real concurrent connections/API instances, role changes, scope changes, grant revocation, rollback and pool cleanup. Current evidence is deterministic service/guard scheduling, not a concurrent HTTP race test. Project removal need not revoke every unrelated org session if current authority is safely fenced otherwise.
findings.evidence_level: TARGETED_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION; see report for HTTP versus guard/service limits; not independent acceptance

findings.requirement: Complete and validate the project-role catalogue
findings.acceptance: Each approved project role contributes its intended capability only within its project and narrower resource scope. Org SITE/project QC can perform an eligible QC review but cannot decide unrelated requirements. Cover aliases, unknown/malformed roles, reviewer-role matching, assignment, self-approval and multi-project role changes. The read-route permission defect in 012 is related but does not supply the missing QC decision capability.

findings.requirement: Resolve indirect resources before evaluating project capabilities
findings.acceptance: Equivalent nested/direct routes agree for legitimate and forbidden actors. Test review, document/version, asset, requirement, package and submission aliases; forged project IDs; mixed bulk IDs; and concurrent role changes. Fixing a GET decorator alone does not repair other direct actions that depend on a project-derived capability.

Valid IDs retain scope and pool cleanup; direct/nested routes agree. Cover relevant guest and member routes. Cross-reference original G01-016; this report does not mark it accepted.

findings.requirement: Restore a safe legitimate external evidence-read workflow
findings.acceptance: A legitimately authorized client/consultant can inspect the exact eligible contractor version and its permitted review data. Unapproved drafts, superseded versions, another supplier/project/tenant, expired/revoked grants and missing independent authority for decisions remain blocked. No upload capability workaround. This audit did not seed a fake approved engineering document or legal delegation to manufacture a positive integration result. Positive storage/browser/external acceptance remains unperformed and must be supplied honestly with the relevant groups.
